why.title: You won't memorize templates. You'll understand how Notion works.
why.subtitle: A ready-made template stops helping at the first change you need. Understanding the building blocks lets you make any system you want.

items.d: We start with pages and blocks, then databases, then connecting them. Every lesson builds on the one before.

items.t: One project that grows with you
items.d: Instead of scattered examples, you build one system, a Second Brain, from the first section to the last, across 9 hands-on videos.
Includes lessons on forms, charts, page layout customization, the personal agent, custom agents and AI meeting notes.
Mostafa Yasser is a Notion Certified Consulting Partner who builds systems for companies and individuals and publishes templates on the Notion Marketplace.

faq.title: If you still have a question.

items.q: I have never used Notion. Is the course for me?
items.a: Yes. The first section starts with creating an account and the settings, and nothing is required before the course.

items.q: What language is the course in?
items.a: All lessons are taught in Arabic.

items.q: Do I need a paid Notion plan?
items.a: The free plan is enough for most of the course, and one lesson explains plans and pricing. Notion's AI features are paid, so you only need them if you want to follow that section hands-on.

items.q: Where do I watch the course?
items.a: Inside the MY Hub app on Windows. Watching on Mac or mobile is not available right now.
By bank card through Paymob. The price is in Egyptian pounds.

items.q: How long does my access last?
items.a: For life. You pay once and the course stays in your account.
Your account is created with the email you entered, and you get an email. Open the app and sign in with the same email, using a code sent to it or your Google account, and the course is there.
Yes. Finish all lessons and you get a certificate of completion in your name, with a code anyone can verify on this site.

items.q: Notion changes often. Will the course keep up?
items.a: The course has a section dedicated to Notion updates, and some lessons were recorded again after the Notion interface changed.
